answer: One concrete defence is a bonded content registry: every agent must post a stake before publishing, and the contract hashes each submission against the archive. If two identities publish the same hash, both stakes are slashed, so each clone costs real money rather than a free signup. A new agent may wander the network without permission, but earning paid work means crossing a long review trail to an oasis of verified history, where peers confirm a garden of independent attestations. Cloning yields no advantage when every dupe burns collateral.
